Lessons.Title: Interpreting and Creating Graphs
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: use a complex or ambiguous verbal description to design a plausible graph, label features and justify assumptions; interpret average rate in context. First-party Edulytiks adaptation based on Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 4 Lesson 8, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/4/8/preparation.html and student tasks at https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/4/8/index.html (CC BY 4.0). Official Addressing HSF-IF.B.4 and HSF-IF.B.6. The original activities involve flag-raising and descriptions/video; text examples here preserve modeling without claiming access to source clips.

Independent original flag-raising scenario: a flag starts at 0 metres, rises uniformly to 6 metres between t=0 and t=3 seconds, stays fixed at 6m until t=8, then lowers uniformly to 0m by t=11. The height H(t) is a piecewise-linear *model*, not an observation of a real flag. Its anchors are (0,0),(3,6),(8,6),(11,0); a learner connects these with straight lines, units and an explicitly stated assumption of constant speed in each moving interval.

Piecewise function for 0≤t≤11: H(t)=2t for 0≤t≤3; H(t)=6 for 3≤t≤8; H(t)=22−2t for 8≤t≤11. At t=3 both first two formulas give6, at t=8 both final formulas give6. Upward speed 2m/s, rest speed0m/s, downward rate −2m/s; all heights remain nonnegative.

Modeling variation: if the flag briefly pauses at half height on the way up, a graph consistent with that new description gains an extra horizontal segment. More than one graph may satisfy a vague verbal account; student must identify what is known, what is inferred and which assumptions determine the shape.

Student activity: draw two different plausible graphs from an underspecified situation, label intercepts/maxima/constant intervals and explain their common and different features. State that actual publisher video clips are not supplied in this first-party JSON; do not imply a video was watched or produced. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each for faithful context model, accurate graph/features and rates, explicit assumptions, and critique of an alternative valid graph.

KeyConcepts.Title: Model from a description
KeyConcepts.Definition: A graph can encode start, stop, increasing and decreasing stages inferred from narrative.
KeyConcepts.Rule: List milestones and avoid invented instantaneous dynamics.

KeyConcepts.Title: Piecewise graph
KeyConcepts.Definition: Different mathematical rules apply to separate input intervals.

KeyConcepts.Title: Ambiguity
KeyConcepts.Definition: A verbal description may not uniquely determine a graph without assumptions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Distinguish measured facts from modeling choices.
KeyConcepts.Example: A flag could accelerate rather than rise at constant speed while reaching the same height in3s.

WorkedExamples.Title: Write height rule in phases
WorkedExamples.Question: Model flag up, pause and down using anchors (0,0),(3,6),(8,6),(11,0).
WorkedExamples.Method: Connect a labelled original graph or table to exact values; verify calculations independently.
Steps: Initial rise slope (6−0)/(3−0)=2m/s, so H=2t on [0,3].
Between3 and8 height is fixed at6.
Line through (8,6) with slope −2 has rule H(t)=6−2(t−8)=22−2t.

WorkedExamples.Title: Interpret graph intervals
WorkedExamples.Question: When is flag stationary and what is maximum height?
WorkedExamples.Method: Connect a labelled original graph or table to exact values; verify calculations independently.
Steps: It is horizontal from3s to8s, a five-second pause.
It then falls to zero at11s.
Maximum output is6m at every time in [3,8].

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare an alternative motion
WorkedExamples.Question: Could the flag accelerate upward but still reach6m at3s?
WorkedExamples.Method: Connect a labelled original graph or table to exact values; verify calculations independently.
Steps: The two endpoint facts (0,0),(3,6) constrain net rise only.
A curved increasing graph could also join the endpoints.
Such a graph would not have constant instantaneous rate.
State an acceleration assumption explicitly before changing the model.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Yes; endpoint data allow multiple paths with same average rate.
WorkedExamples.Check: No exact intermediate heights were supplied.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Presenting a chosen sketch as the only permissible graph
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Ambiguous input descriptions allow alternative interpolations.
CommonMistakes.Correction: List assumptions and accept consistent alternatives.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The flag may stop while elevated.
The lesson's first-party JSON has no verified video playback.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Disclose demonstration is a text-based original simulation.

SummaryPoints: A graph from a narrative requires known milestones and explicit assumptions.
A piecewise model can represent increasing, constant and decreasing intervals.
Rate of change and key features can be described without pretending the underlying motion was measured.
Teacher reviews alternate defensible sketches and their limitations.
